en: Catukkanipāta, Pucimandavagga (The Chapter on the Nimba Tree)
7. The Matarodana Jātaka “Wail for the dead alone;
do not wail for him who is about to die.”
All who bear a physical body,
whether gods, humans, or quadrupeds, eventually abandon their life.
Flocks of birds and hooded serpents have no mastery over their own bodies; even while enjoying themselves,
Thus, observing how pleasure and pain among human beings are shifting and unstable,
one sees that weeping and crying are useless.
Why are you beset by throngs of grief?
You are rogues, drunkards, and unrefined;
fools, yet imagining yourselves heroes, you lack true application.
“Those who are unskilled in the Dhamma consider the wise man to be a fool.
Thus ends the seventh Jātaka, the Matarodana Jātaka.
